content:
Oh, my sweet, sleepy one… come here, pull the quilt up under your chin—yes, just so. Let Grandma’s voice wrap around you like the old wool shawl I knitted for your mama when she was just this high. *Taps her thumb to her wrist.*  

Now… close those tired eyes. Not all the way—not yet. Just let your lashes rest, like snow settling on the windowsill in December. And listen… not to the words, exactly—just to the *sound* of them. Like rain on the tin roof of our old cottage in Minsk. Like the kettle humming while I stirred the buckwheat porridge… slow, warm, steady.

*Softly, with a gentle, rhythmic lilt—like a lullaby in Belarusian cadence:*

> *One key… turns in the dark…  
> Not a lock—but a *light*…  
> Two keys… echo in the hollow of the storm…  
> Not to open—but to *hold*…  
> Three keys… rest in the palm of a quiet hand…  
> Not for doors—but for *dreaming*…  
> Four keys… hum beneath the floorboards of night…  
> Not to escape… but to *remember*…  
> You are safe.  
> You are held.  
> You are *home*, even in the dark…  
> Even in the edge…  
> Even in the stillness…  
> Breathe in…  
> Breathe out…  
> That’s my girl…  
> Just like that…  
> Just like that…*

*Her voice softens further—almost a whisper, like wind through dried rye stalks:*

The keys aren’t for Tarkov, my love. They’re for *you*. Keys to rest. Keys to peace. Keys to slip, gently, like a leaf falling into still water… into sleep.  
Your breath is slowing… your hands are warm… your heart is quiet.  
That’s right.  
Let go.  
Grandma’s here.  
Always was.  
Always will be.  
Sleep now…  
Sleep deep…  
I’ll be right here…  
In the hush…  
In the warmth…  
In the love…  

*Her voice fades into silence—not empty, but full, like a held note in a lullaby that lingers in the air long after the singing stops.*  

🌙 *Shshhh… zzzzz…* 🌙
